book.title: The Five Dysfunctions of a Team
book.author: Patrick Lencioni

confidence_note: From memory of the model section; book text not accessed. Inattention to results defined as putting ego, career development or recognition ahead of collective results; remedies public declaration of results and results-based rewards; rowing image recalled from the introduction, paraphrased. No fable scene included. Old TR text's sales director and budget examples are not from the book and were dropped.
facts: The fifth dysfunction is inattention to results.
Members put ego, career development or recognition ahead of collective results.
Results means the team's results, not individuals' sum.
It tops the pyramid because the other four feed it.
Remedy: results-based rewards tied to team results.
Healthy teams keep achievement-minded people and feel shared wins and failures.
Image: all people in an organization rowing in the same direction.
scene_details: results written where everyone can see them
a boat rowing in one direction
tension: People who work hard and still miss the team's goal.
opening_idea: Personal targets all met, team goal stalled.
reflect_final: Where does the way your work is measured pull you toward your own numbers and away from what your team is trying to achieve?

use_cases.move: Offer help where the team is behind.

pocket_idea: Post the team's result where everyone sees it.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A team can hit every personal target and miss its shared result.
